title: Netflix Data Analysis
summary: Exploratory analysis of movie metadata, genres, release patterns, popularity, and feature relationships.
problem: Exploration needs a focused way to inspect distributions and relationships before deciding what is worth modeling.
solution: A notebook-based analysis turns catalog metadata into readable views of genres, release patterns, popularity, and feature relationships.
architecture: Case-study context: The lab explores how a streaming catalog can be profiled through metadata, genres, release patterns, popularity, and feature relationships.
Dataset preparation: Python and pandas provide the notebook-friendly loading, cleaning, and reshaping path. Components: Python, pandas, Jupyter.
Exploration: Matplotlib and seaborn turn catalog fields into distributions, comparisons, and relationship views. Components: Matplotlib, seaborn.
Interpretation: The final output remains exploratory analysis: a compact lab for asking better questions of metadata, not a prediction product. Components: Python, Jupyter.
The README describes a Kaggle-sourced movie catalog explored with Python and pandas.
The notebook workflow cleans data types, handles missing values/outliers, and explores release dates, genres, popularity, vote counts, and vote averages.
Matplotlib and seaborn visualize distributions and relationships; the portfolio explicitly frames the work as exploratory rather than predictive.
outcomes: Kept Netflix as the single compact data-analysis lab in the public catalog.
Presented it as exploratory analysis rather than predictive modeling.
